query: How can we improve incident resolution efficiency?

per_column.name: incident_category
per_column.rationale: Categorizes free-text short_description into meaningful incident types, giving a strong axis to group resolution efficiency by category. Sample values (printer, network_or_vpn, database) are sound readings of the source text.

per_column.name: affected_component
per_column.rationale: Well-grounded extraction of the affected hardware/software component, but for most rows it closely mirrors incident_category (printer->printer, database->database), reducing independent analytical leverage. Still adds some granularity (keyboard vs mouse, workstation).

per_column.name: failure_symptom
per_column.rationale: Symptom taxonomy (not_responding, not_connecting, physical_failure) is a genuinely new axis orthogonal to component, useful for correlating symptom type with resolution time. Samples map reasonably from the text, though 'not_responding' for a generic 'not working' description is a somewhat loose but defensible inference.

per_column.name: resolution_action_type
per_column.rationale: Resolution action type is directly relevant to improving resolution efficiency. However the source text (short_description of the problem) rarely states the resolution taken; values like 'repair_needed' or 'connectivity_fix' are inferred from the problem statement, not from any resolution field, so many values are unwarranted confident specifics.

per_column.name: involves_escalation_or_reassignment
per_column.rationale: Escalation/reassignment is highly relevant to efficiency, but the sampled source text (short_description + timestamps) contains no evidence of escalation or reassignment. Two near-identical printer rows get opposite true/false values with no supporting text, indicating fabricated/ungrounded assignment.

per_column.name: is_recurring_issue_type
per_column.rationale: Constant 'true' for all 500 rows — no analytical variance and no discriminating value. Also not derivable from the per-row source text; recurrence cannot be asserted uniformly and is essentially fabricated.

per_column.name: software_trigger_indicated
per_column.rationale: A software-vs-hardware trigger flag could help slice causes, but it is largely a coarse binary derivable from category and is a confident inference the short text often does not explicitly support. Values in samples (mostly false) are plausible but weakly grounded.

judge.rationale: The augmentation adds several genuinely useful axes (incident_category, failure_symptom, resolution_action_type) for analyzing resolution efficiency, and the categorization columns are well grounded in the short_description text. However groundedness is dragged down by columns that assert facts absent from the source: resolution_action_type and involves_escalation_or_reassignment are inferred from problem statements without resolution/escalation evidence (near-identical rows get opposite flags), and is_recurring_issue_type is a constant 'true' that is both analytically inert and fabricated. affected_component is largely redundant with incident_category.
